title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 201 (Forms of, and procedure in relation to, certain applications)

content.overview: Section 201 provides that every application made to the Central Government under Chapter XIII (appointment and remuneration of managerial personnel) shall be in such form as may be prescribed. Before any application is made by a company to the Central Government under that Chapter, there shall be issued by or on behalf of the company a general notice to the members indicating the nature of the application proposed to be made. Such notice shall be published at least once in a newspaper in the principal language of the district and circulating in that district where the registered office is situate and at least once in English in an English newspaper circulating in that district. Copies of the notices and a certificate of due publication are attached to the application. Objections received are also forwarded.
content.glance: CG applications under managerial-personnel Chapter: prescribed form; prior general notice to members; newspaper publication (local language + English); copies and due-publication certificate with application; objections forwarded.
content.study: Every application made to the Central Government under this Chapter shall be in such form as may be prescribed. (1) Before any application is made by a company to the Central Government under any of the sections aforesaid, there shall be issued by or on behalf of the company a general notice to the members thereof, indicating the nature of the application proposed to be made. (2) Such notice shall be published at least once in a newspaper in the principal language of the district in which the registered office of the company is situate and circulating in that district, and at least once in English in an English newspaper circulating in that district. (3) The copies of the notices, together with a certificate by the company as to the due publication thereof, shall be attached to the application. (4) Any objections received shall be forwarded with the application. Current-law framing: identify an application to the Central Government under the managerial-personnel Chapter; use the prescribed form; issue and publish the general notice; attach proof and objections. Substantive conditions remain in ss. 196, 197 and Schedule V; s. 201 is procedural.

sections.heading: Prescribed Form
sections.body: Every application to the Central Government under the managerial-personnel Chapter must be in the prescribed form.

sections.heading: General Notice to Members
sections.body: Before the application, the company issues a general notice to members indicating the nature of the proposed application.

sections.heading: Newspaper Publication
sections.body: Notice published at least once in a newspaper in the principal language of the district of the registered office, and at least once in English in an English newspaper circulating in that district.

sections.heading: Attachments
sections.body: Copies of the notices and a certificate of due publication are attached; objections received are forwarded with the application.

provisions.title: Forms of, and procedure in relation to, certain applications

examples.title: Missing newspaper notice
examples.body: A company applies to the Central Government for approval of MD remuneration but publishes no newspaper notice to members. Section 201 requires prior general notice by newspaper publication in the local language and in English, with proof attached to the application.

examples.title: Objections forwarded
examples.body: Members object in response to the general notice. Those objections must be forwarded with the application under s. 201.

hypotheticals.question: Does compliance with s. 201 guarantee Central Government approval of the remuneration?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 201 is procedural (form, notice, publication, attachments). Substantive approval conditions remain in sections 196, 197, 200 and Schedule V.

distinctions.title: Application procedure (s. 201) vs remuneration ceilings (s. 197)
distinctions.left: Form, notice and publication for CG applications

misconceptions.trap: A Board resolution alone is enough to send a managerial-remuneration application to the Central Government.
misconceptions.correction: Section 201 requires the prescribed form, prior general notice to members with newspaper publication, and attachment of proof and objections.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 201 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify CG application under the Chapter. II. Check prescribed form. III. Test general notice and newspaper publication. IV. Confirm attachments and objections. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Application facts; notice/publication proof; objections; precise relief.

examTips: Prior general notice + dual newspaper publication.
